# Authentication

* API Key (cookieAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **sessionid**, in: cookie.

* API Key (tokenAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **Authorization**, in: header. `Token <token>` (v1) or `Bearer <key>.<token>` (v2)

## dcim_connected_device_list

<a id="opIddcim_connected_device_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8000/api/dcim/connected-device/?peer_device=string&peer_interface=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Cookie: sessionid=${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/dcim/connected-device/`

This endpoint allows a user to determine what device (if any) is connected to a given peer device and peer
interface. This is useful in a situation where a device boots with no configuration, but can detect its neighbors
via a protocol such as LLDP. Two query parameters must be included in the request:

* `peer_device`: The name of the peer device
* `peer_interface`: The name of the peer interface

<h3 id="dcimconnecteddevicelist-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brief|query|boolean|false|Return only brief fields for each object.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response. Example: `fields=id,name`.|
|omit|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of fields to exclude from the response. Example: `omit=description,tags`.|
|peer_device|query|string|true|The name of the peer device|
|peer_interface|query|string|true|The name of the peer interface|

## dcim_devices_render_config_create

<a id="opIddcim_devices_render_config_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/dcim/devices/0/render-config/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Cookie: sessionid=${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "config_template_id": 0
  }'
```

`POST /api/dcim/devices/{id}/render-config/`

Resolve and render the preferred ConfigTemplate for this Device or Virtual Machine.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "config_template_id": 0
}
```

<h3 id="dcimdevicesrenderconfigcreate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|format|query|string|false|none|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|A unique integer value identifying this device.|
|body|body|[RenderConfigInputRequest](#schemarenderconfiginputrequest)|false|none|
|» config_template_id|body|integer(int64)|false|Optional ID of the ConfigTemplate to render. If omitted, the object's assigned config template is used.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|format|json|
|format|txt|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "configtemplate": {
    "id": 0,
    "url": "http://example.com",
    "display": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string"
  },
  "content": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "property1": null,
  "property2": null
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "property1": null,
  "property2": null
}
```

<h3 id="dcimdevicesrenderconfigcreate-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The rendered config template. When the client requests `text/plain`, the raw rendered content is returned in place of the JSON object.|[RenderedConfig](#schemarenderedconfig)|
|400|Bad Request|No config template could be resolved for this object.|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|An error occurred while rendering the config template.|Inline|

<h3 id="dcimdevicesrenderconfigcreate-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|

Status Code **500**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
cookieAuth, tokenAuth
</aside>

cookieAuth, tokenAuth

## dcim_interface_templates_destroy

<a id="opIddcim_interface_templates_destroy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/dcim/interface-templates/0/ \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Cookie: sessionid=${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /api/dcim/interface-templates/{id}/`

Delete a interface template object.

<h3 id="dciminterfacetemplatesdestroy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|A unique integer value identifying this interface template.|

<h3 id="dciminterfacetemplatesdestroy-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No response body|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
cookieAuth, tokenAuth
</aside>

```bash
  }'
```

## dcim_interfaces_list

<a id="opIddcim_interfaces_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/dcim/interfaces/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Cookie: sessionid=${API_KEY}"
```

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
cookieAuth, tokenAuth
</aside>

## dcim_interfaces_trace_retrieve

<a id="opIddcim_interfaces_trace_retrieve"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/dcim/interfaces/0/trace/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Cookie: sessionid=${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/dcim/interfaces/{id}/trace/`

Trace a complete cable path and return each segment as a three-tuple of (termination, cable, termination).

<h3 id="dciminterfacestraceretrieve-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brief|query|boolean|false|Return only brief fields for each object.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response. Example: `fields=id,name`.|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|A unique integer value identifying this interface.|
|omit|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of fields to exclude from the response. Example: `omit=description,tags`.|

|» *oneOf*|body|[WritableServiceTemplateRequest](#schemawritableservicetemplaterequest)|false|Shared port-mapping handling for the Service and ServiceTemplate serializers, including backward<br>compatibility for the legacy single-protocol ``protocol``/``ports`` representation.<br><br>Read: alongside the ``port_mappings`` list, a service that uses a single protocol also reports the<br>legacy ``protocol`` and ``ports`` fields; a multi-protocol service reports ``null`` for both (it<br>cannot be expressed in the old single-protocol format).<br><br>Write: either format is accepted. When the legacy ``protocol``/``ports`` pair is supplied (and<br>``port_mappings`` is not), it is translated into ``port_mappings``. Supplying both together is<br>accepted only when the legacy fields agree with what ``port_mappings`` implies (e.g. a full-object<br>round-trip that echoes back the read representation); a genuine conflict is rejected as ambiguous.<br><br>Subclassing ``serializers.Serializer`` (rather than a plain mixin) lets DRF's metaclass collect the<br>fields declared here into the inheriting serializers.|

When the legacy ``protocol``/``ports`` pair is supplied (and<br>``port_mappings`` is not), it is translated into ``port_mappings``. Supplying both together is<br>accepted only when the legacy fields agree with what ``port_mappings`` implies (e.g. a full-object<br>round-trip that echoes back the read representation); a genuine conflict is rejected as ambiguous.<br><br>Subclassing ``serializers.Serializer`` (rather than a plain mixin) lets DRF's metaclass collect the<br>fields declared here into the inheriting serializers.|

The validated write is centralized<br>on the interface model (BaseInterface.set_primary_mac_address); this mixin is a thin adapter that<br>owns the permission check, the shortcut-vs-primary_mac_address conflict guard, and translating the<br>model's validation errors into API errors.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[[WritableVMInterfaceRequest](#schemawritablevminterfacerequest)]|false|none|

<h2 id="tocS_Bookmark">Bookmark</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabookmark"></a>

```json
  "url": "http://example.com",
  "display": "string",

  "object": null,

    "id": 0,
    "url": "http://example.com",
    "display": "string",
    "username": "string"
  },
  "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64)|true|read-only|none|
|url|string(uri)|true|read-only|none|
|display|string|true|read-only|none|
|object_type|string|true|none|none|
|object_id|integer(int64)|true|none|none|
|object|object \| null|true|read-only|none|
|user|[BriefUser](#schemabriefuser)|true|none|Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during<br>validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)<br><br>Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values<br>must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()<br>wrote.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|read-only|none|

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64)|true|read-only|none|
|url|string(uri)|true|read-only|none|
|display|string|true|read-only|none|
|name|string|true|none|{module} is accepted as a substitution for the module bay position when attached to a module type.|
|description|string|false|none|none|

```json
  "display": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

|name|string|true|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|none|

```json
  },
```


Mixin for Interface and VMInterface serializers that adds a `mac_address` shortcut field for
creating/updating the primary MACAddress in a single request. The validated write is centralized
on the interface model (BaseInterface.set_primary_mac_address); this mixin is a thin adapter that
owns the permission check, the shortcut-vs-primary_mac_address conflict guard, and translating the
model's validation errors into API errors.

|name|string|true|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|none|

|_occupied|boolean|true|read-only|none|

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64)|true|read-only|none|
|url|string(uri)|true|read-only|none|
|display|string|true|read-only|none|
|name|string|true|none|{module} is accepted as a substitution for the module bay position when attached to a module type.|
|description|string|false|none|none|

```json
  "url": "http://example.com",
  "display": "string",
  "username": "string"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64)|true|read-only|none|
|url|string(uri)|true|read-only|none|
|display|string|true|read-only|none|
|username|string|true|none|Required. 150 characters or fewer. Letters, digits and @/./+/-/_ only.|

```json
  "object_type": "string",
  "object_id": 0,
  "user": 0
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

|object_type|string|true|none|none|

|user|integer(int64) \| [BriefUserRequest](#schemabriefuserrequest)|true|none|none|

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

Mixin for Interface and VMInterface serializers that adds a `mac_address` shortcut field for
creating/updating the primary MACAddress in a single request. The validated write is centralized
on the interface model (BaseInterface.set_primary_mac_address); this mixin is a thin adapter that
owns the permission check, the shortcut-vs-primary_mac_address conflict guard, and translating the
model's validation errors into API errors.

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "device_type": 0,
  "module_type": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "type": "virtual",
  "channels": 1,
  "channel_id": 1,
  "enabled": true,
  "mgmt_only": true,
  "description": "string",
  "parent": {
    "name": "string"
  },
  "bridge": {
    "name": "string"
  },
  "poe_mode": "pd",
  "poe_type": "type1-ieee802.3af",
  "rf_role": "ap"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.


The failure of a single object within a bulk operation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64)|false|none|The ID of the object which failed. Present once the entry has been matched to an object; mutually exclusive with `index`.|
|index|integer|false|none|The zero-based position of the entry within the submitted list. Used where no object has been identified for the entry: always for creations, and for updates and deletions where the entry itself could not be interpreted (e.g. a missing or non-numeric `id`). Mutually exclusive with `id`.|
|errors|object|true|none|The errors for this entry, keyed by field name. Values are ordinarily arrays of messages. Errors which pertain to no particular field -- model validation, protection rules, restricted tags, object-level permissions, or the shape of the entry itself -- all appear under the single key `__all__`.|

responsible for it.

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "device_type": 0,
  "module_type": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "type": "iec-60320-c5",
  "color": "string",
  "power_port": 0,
  "feed_leg": "A",
  "description": "string"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

```json
  "id": 0,
  "device_type": 0,
  "module_type": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "type": "iec-60320-c6",
  "maximum_draw": 1,
  "allocated_draw": 1,
  "description": "string"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

<h2 id="tocS_BulkRearPortTemplateRequest">BulkRearPortTemplateRequest</h2>

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "device_type": 0,
  "module_type": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "type": "8p8c",
  "color": "string",
  "positions": 1,
  "front_ports": [
    {
      "position": 0,
      "front_port": 0,
      "front_port_position": 1
    }
  ],
  "description": "string"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64)|true|none|none|
|device_type|integer(int64) \| object \| null|false|none|none|
|module_type|integer(int64) \| object \| null|false|none|none|

Shared port-mapping handling for the Service and ServiceTemplate serializers, including backward
compatibility for the legacy single-protocol ``protocol``/``ports`` representation.

Read: alongside the ``port_mappings`` list, a service that uses a single protocol also reports the
legacy ``protocol`` and ``ports`` fields; a multi-protocol service reports ``null`` for both (it
cannot be expressed in the old single-protocol format).

Write: either format is accepted. When the legacy ``protocol``/``ports`` pair is supplied (and
``port_mappings`` is not), it is translated into ``port_mappings``. Supplying both together is
accepted only when the legacy fields agree with what ``port_mappings`` implies (e.g. a full-object
round-trip that echoes back the read representation); a genuine conflict is rejected as ambiguous.

Subclassing ``serializers.Serializer`` (rather than a plain mixin) lets DRF's metaclass collect the
fields declared here into the inheriting serializers.

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

wrote.

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

<a id="tocSdevicebaytemplaterequest"></a>

```json
{
  "device_type": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "enabled": true,
  "description": "string"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|device_type|integer(int64) \| [BriefDeviceTypeRequest](#schemabriefdevicetyperequest)|true|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|{module} is accepted as a substitution for the module bay position when attached to a module type.|
|label|string|false|none|Physical label|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|none|

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

### Properties

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

|module_type|object \| null|false|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|{module} is accepted as a substitution for the module bay position when attached to a module type.|

<h2 id="tocS_Notification">Notification</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanotification"></a>
<a id="schema_Notification"></a>
<a id="tocSnotification"></a>
<a id="tocsnotification"></a>

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "url": "http://example.com",
  "display": "string",
  "object_type": "string",
  "object_id": 0,
  "object": null,
  "user": {
    "id": 0,
    "url": "http://example.com",
    "display": "string",
    "username": "string"
  },
  "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "read": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "event_type": "object_created"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64)|true|read-only|none|
|url|string(uri)|true|read-only|none|
|display|string|true|read-only|none|
|object_type|string|true|none|none|
|object_id|integer(int64)|true|none|none|
|object|object \| null|true|read-only|none|
|user|[BriefUser](#schemabriefuser)|true|none|Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during<br>validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)<br><br>Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values<br>must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()<br>wrote.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|read-only|none|
|read|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|none|
|event_type|string|true|none|* `object_created` - Object created<br>* `object_updated` - Object updated<br>* `object_deleted` - Object deleted<br>* `job_started` - Job started<br>* `job_completed` - Job completed<br>* `job_failed` - Job failed<br>* `job_errored` - Job errored|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|event_type|object_created|
|event_type|object_updated|
|event_type|object_deleted|
|event_type|job_started|
|event_type|job_completed|
|event_type|job_failed|
|event_type|job_errored|

```json
  "object_id": 0,
```
```json
  "user": 0
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.


Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.


Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

|description|string|false|none|none|

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

|image|string(binary)|false|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|none|

Mixin for Interface and VMInterface serializers that adds a `mac_address` shortcut field for
creating/updating the primary MACAddress in a single request. The validated write is centralized
on the interface model (BaseInterface.set_primary_mac_address); this mixin is a thin adapter that
owns the permission check, the shortcut-vs-primary_mac_address conflict guard, and translating the
model's validation errors into API errors.

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "device_type": 0,
  "module_type": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "type": "virtual",
  "channels": 1,
  "channel_id": 1,
  "enabled": true,
  "mgmt_only": true,
  "description": "string",
  "parent": {
    "name": "string"
  },
  "bridge": {
    "name": "string"
  },
  "poe_mode": "pd",
  "poe_type": "type1-ieee802.3af",
  "rf_role": "ap"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

|name|string|false|none|{module} is accepted as a substitution for the module bay position when attached to a module type.|
|label|string|false|none|Physical label|

```json
  "device_type": 0,
  "parent": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "role": 0,
  "manufacturer": 0,
  "part_id": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "component_type": "string",
  "component_id": 0
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64)|true|none|none|
|device_type|integer(int64) \| [BriefDeviceTypeRequest](#schemabriefdevicetyperequest)|false|none|none|
|parent|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|none|
|name|string|false|none|{module} is accepted as a substitution for the module bay position when attached to a module type.|

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

Shared port-mapping handling for the Service and ServiceTemplate serializers, including backward
compatibility for the legacy single-protocol ``protocol``/``ports`` representation.

Read: alongside the ``port_mappings`` list, a service that uses a single protocol also reports the
legacy ``protocol`` and ``ports`` fields; a multi-protocol service reports ``null`` for both (it
cannot be expressed in the old single-protocol format).

Write: either format is accepted. When the legacy ``protocol``/``ports`` pair is supplied (and
``port_mappings`` is not), it is translated into ``port_mappings``. Supplying both together is
accepted only when the legacy fields agree with what ``port_mappings`` implies (e.g. a full-object
round-trip that echoes back the read representation); a genuine conflict is rejected as ambiguous.

Subclassing ``serializers.Serializer`` (rather than a plain mixin) lets DRF's metaclass collect the
fields declared here into the inheriting serializers.

<h2 id="tocS_PatchedBulkUserRequest">PatchedBulkUserRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapatchedbulkuserrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_PatchedBulkUserRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSpatchedbulkuserrequest"></a>
<a id="tocspatchedbulkuserrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "username": "string",
  "password": "string",
  "first_name": "string",
  "last_name": "string",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "is_active": true,
  "date_joined": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "last_login": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "groups": [
    0
  ],
  "permissions": [
    0
  ]
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64)|true|none|none|
|username|string|false|none|Required. 150 characters or fewer. Letters, digits and @/./+/-/_ only.|
|password|string|false|write-only|none|
|first_name|string|false|none|none|
|last_name|string|false|none|none|
|email|string(email) \| string|false|none|none|
|is_active|boolean|false|none|Designates whether this user should be treated as active. Unselect this instead of deleting accounts.|
|date_joined|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|last_login|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|none|
|groups|[integer(int64)]|false|none|none|
|permissions|[integer(int64)]|false|none|none|

Mixin for Interface and VMInterface serializers that adds a `mac_address` shortcut field for
creating/updating the primary MACAddress in a single request. The validated write is centralized
on the interface model (BaseInterface.set_primary_mac_address); this mixin is a thin adapter that
owns the permission check, the shortcut-vs-primary_mac_address conflict guard, and translating the
model's validation errors into API errors.

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.


Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

Mixin for Interface and VMInterface serializers that adds a `mac_address` shortcut field for
creating/updating the primary MACAddress in a single request. The validated write is centralized
on the interface model (BaseInterface.set_primary_mac_address); this mixin is a thin adapter that
owns the permission check, the shortcut-vs-primary_mac_address conflict guard, and translating the
model's validation errors into API errors.

<a id="tocspatchedwritableinterfacetemplaterequest"></a>

```json
{
  "device_type": 0,
  "module_type": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "type": "virtual",
  "channels": 1,
  "channel_id": 1,
  "enabled": true,
  "mgmt_only": true,
  "description": "string",
  "parent": 0,
  "bridge": 0,
  "poe_mode": "pd",
  "poe_type": "type1-ieee802.3af",
  "rf_role": "ap"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

|module_type|integer(int64) \| object \| null|false|none|none|
|name|string|false|none|{module} is accepted as a substitution for the module bay position when attached to a module type.|
|label|string|false|none|Physical label|


Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

```json
{
  "device_type": 0,
  "module_type": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "type": "iec-60320-c6",
  "maximum_draw": 1,
  "allocated_draw": 1,
  "description": "string"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

```json
    "property2": null

```

Shared port-mapping handling for the Service and ServiceTemplate serializers, including backward
compatibility for the legacy single-protocol ``protocol``/``ports`` representation.

Read: alongside the ``port_mappings`` list, a service that uses a single protocol also reports the
legacy ``protocol`` and ``ports`` fields; a multi-protocol service reports ``null`` for both (it
cannot be expressed in the old single-protocol format).

Write: either format is accepted. When the legacy ``protocol``/``ports`` pair is supplied (and
``port_mappings`` is not), it is translated into ``port_mappings``. Supplying both together is
accepted only when the legacy fields agree with what ``port_mappings`` implies (e.g. a full-object
round-trip that echoes back the read representation); a genuine conflict is rejected as ambiguous.

Subclassing ``serializers.Serializer`` (rather than a plain mixin) lets DRF's metaclass collect the
fields declared here into the inheriting serializers.

Mixin for Interface and VMInterface serializers that adds a `mac_address` shortcut field for
creating/updating the primary MACAddress in a single request. The validated write is centralized
on the interface model (BaseInterface.set_primary_mac_address); this mixin is a thin adapter that
owns the permission check, the shortcut-vs-primary_mac_address conflict guard, and translating the
model's validation errors into API errors.

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

### Properties

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64)|true|read-only|none|
|display|string|true|read-only|none|
|file_path|string|true|read-only|none|
|created|string(date-time)|true|read-only|none|
|last_updated|string(date-time) \| null|true|read-only|none|

Shared port-mapping handling for the Service and ServiceTemplate serializers, including backward
compatibility for the legacy single-protocol ``protocol``/``ports`` representation.

Read: alongside the ``port_mappings`` list, a service that uses a single protocol also reports the
legacy ``protocol`` and ``ports`` fields; a multi-protocol service reports ``null`` for both (it
cannot be expressed in the old single-protocol format).

Write: either format is accepted. When the legacy ``protocol``/``ports`` pair is supplied (and
``port_mappings`` is not), it is translated into ``port_mappings``. Supplying both together is
accepted only when the legacy fields agree with what ``port_mappings`` implies (e.g. a full-object
round-trip that echoes back the read representation); a genuine conflict is rejected as ambiguous.

Subclassing ``serializers.Serializer`` (rather than a plain mixin) lets DRF's metaclass collect the
fields declared here into the inheriting serializers.

creating/updating the primary MACAddress in a single request. The validated write is centralized

model's validation errors into API errors.

```json
  "module_type": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "type": "8p8c",
  "color": "string",
  "positions": 1,
  "rear_ports": [
    {
      "position": 0,
      "rear_port": 0,
      "rear_port_position": 1
    }
  ],
  "description": "string"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|device_type|integer(int64) \| object \| null|false|none|none|
|module_type|integer(int64) \| object \| null|false|none|none|

Mixin for Interface and VMInterface serializers that adds a `mac_address` shortcut field for
creating/updating the primary MACAddress in a single request. The validated write is centralized
on the interface model (BaseInterface.set_primary_mac_address); this mixin is a thin adapter that
owns the permission check, the shortcut-vs-primary_mac_address conflict guard, and translating the
model's validation errors into API errors.

```json
{
  "device_type": 0,
  "module_type": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "type": "virtual",
  "channels": 1,
  "channel_id": 1,
  "enabled": true,
  "mgmt_only": true,
  "description": "string",
  "parent": 0,
  "bridge": 0,
  "poe_mode": "pd",
  "poe_type": "type1-ieee802.3af",
  "rf_role": "ap"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

|label|string|false|none|Physical label|

```json

  "device_type": 0,
  "module_type": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "type": "iec-60320-c5",
  "color": "string",
  "power_port": 0,
  "feed_leg": "A",
  "description": "string"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

```json
{
  "device_type": 0,
  "module_type": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "type": "iec-60320-c6",
  "maximum_draw": 1,
  "allocated_draw": 1,
  "description": "string"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

```json
  "module_type": 0,

  "label": "string",
  "type": "8p8c",
  "color": "string",
  "positions": 1,

      "front_port_position": 1
    }
  ],
  "description": "string"
}
```

Extends the built-in ModelSerializer to enforce calling full_clean() on a copy of the associated instance during
validation. (DRF does not do this by default; see https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/issues/3144)

Serializers may declare `model_clean_fields` in Meta, naming scalar model fields whose clean()-normalized values
must reach the database. DRF builds a fresh instance from the validated data on create, discarding what clean()
wrote.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|device_type|integer(int64) \| object \| null|false|none|none|
|module_type|integer(int64) \| object \| null|false|none|none|

Shared port-mapping handling for the Service and ServiceTemplate serializers, including backward
compatibility for the legacy single-protocol ``protocol``/``ports`` representation.

Read: alongside the ``port_mappings`` list, a service that uses a single protocol also reports the
legacy ``protocol`` and ``ports`` fields; a multi-protocol service reports ``null`` for both (it
cannot be expressed in the old single-protocol format).

Write: either format is accepted. When the legacy ``protocol``/``ports`` pair is supplied (and
``port_mappings`` is not), it is translated into ``port_mappings``. Supplying both together is
accepted only when the legacy fields agree with what ``port_mappings`` implies (e.g. a full-object
round-trip that echoes back the read representation); a genuine conflict is rejected as ambiguous.

Subclassing ``serializers.Serializer`` (rather than a plain mixin) lets DRF's metaclass collect the
fields declared here into the inheriting serializers.
